messages:
emma (devex): Support case: user on macOS (M1, brew) ran quickstart, redwoodctl promised token saved to ~/.config/redwood/profiles/default.json but their sample app still gets 401s. any ideas?
rishi (eng-platform): did they install via brew or the universal tarball?
emma (devex): brew cask. they followed docs exactly.
ong (eng-runtime): common culprits: 1) multiple redwoodctl binaries on PATH (one in /usr/local/bin, one in ~/.local/bin) 2) the app running under a different user (launchctl agent) 3) symlinked home dir (e.g., Dropbox).
nina (devops): can we get the output of `which -a redwoodctl` and `ls -la ~/.config/redwood/profiles` from them? also `redwoodctl profile get --active --json` would help.
emma (devex): they pasted logs: 
```
which -a redwoodctl: /usr/local/bin/redwoodctl
ls -la ~/.config/redwood/profiles: shows default.json with token present
app logs: 401 unauthorized when calling /v1/generate
```
rishi (eng-platform): if token exists, maybe it's stale due to rotation. `redwoodctl auth status` should show token exp.
emma (devex): user ran `auth status` and saw token valid for 23 days.
ong (eng-runtime): are we writing token to user XDG file but the SDK used by their sample app reads from RWCTL_PROFILE env or a different config location (legacy ~/.redwood/config.json)? mismatch.
nina (devops): quick check: ask them to run `env | grep RWCTL` and check if RWCTL_PROFILE points to something else.
emma (devex): they returned: no RWCTL_* env set.
rishi (eng-platform): could this be file permission or group ACL where the app process can't read the file? what launches the app?
emma (devex): they used `npm start` for sample, same shell.
ong (eng-runtime): hmm. last idea: macOS sandboxing with symlinked home means realpath differs. Our token loader resolves paths with symlinks and compares inode; if the app resolves to different path it may look up legacy location. I filed a quick hypothesis.
deploy-bot: scheduled a debug session with user on 2026-02-10 16:00 PST
nina (devops): action items: 1) add telemetry when SDK fails to locate profile despite token file present (log attempted paths), 2) make `redwoodctl profile show` print canonical resolved path and perms, 3) docs: call out symlinked homedir caveat.
ong (eng-runtime): i'll add a small change to the profile loader to try both resolved and unresolved paths and emit a helpful error if none match. also ensure permission read errors surface.
emma (devex): thanks! i'll send the support reply with the debug checklist and the symlink note.
